beats.caption: SRAM is the memory built into the GPU die itself
beats.text: Registers, L1 and L2 caches and shared memory on a GPU are SRAM, made in the same logic process as the cores. An H100 carries about 50 MB of L2 plus tens of MB more in registers and L1.

beats.caption: Each bit is six transistors: two inverters holding each other
beats.text: Two inverters are wired in a loop, so each one's output drives the other's input. The loop settles at 0 or 1 and stays there as long as power is on. Two access transistors connect it to the bitlines.

beats.caption: No refresh: the latch holds its bit by itself
beats.text: Unlike a DRAM capacitor, the latch is actively driven, so it never leaks away and needs no refresh. That is why SRAM answers in about a nanosecond, many times faster than HBM.

beats.caption: A read raises the wordline and the cell pulls one bitline down
beats.text: The wordline turns on both access transistors, the side holding 0 pulls its bitline slightly low, and a sense amp reads the difference between BL and BLB. Writes overpower the latch through the same two bitlines.

beats.caption: Fast but big: six transistors per bit versus one plus a capacitor
beats.text: An SRAM bit takes several times the area of a DRAM bit, and SRAM cells have barely shrunk at 3 nm, so on-chip memory is costly die area. Groq and Cerebras build inference chips around huge SRAM in place of HBM. Related: Nvidia (NVDA), TSMC (TSM), Groq (private), Cerebras (CBRS).
